in_text_mentions: puted tomography showed an enlarged right kidney (49.1 × 30.4 mm) with changes in shape; however, the renal pelvis (<2 mm) and medullary part were without significant abnormality. The ureter was dilated throughout its length (cranially 14.4 mm; centrally 19.8 mm; and 6.2 mm in the caudal part at the level of the urinary bladder) and opened into the vagina (Figure 1). The urinary bladder was reduced in size (30.2 × 14.8 mm) without intramural contents, and the left kidney was absent. Conclusion from CT included unilateral renomegaly, hydroureter, ectopic ureter, and agenesis of the left kidney.

in_text_mentions: Imaging studies, including an ultrasound (USG) of the kidneys, ureters, and urinary bladder (KUB), showed a dilated right ureter and a small right kidney. Computed tomography urography (CT urography) further confirmed gross ureteric dilatation consistent with hydro ureter. It detected the ectopic insertion of the tortuous right ureter near the external urethral orifice at the vaginal vestibule alongside an atrophic right kidney. Conversely, the left kidney appeared normal in location, size, and shape (Figures 1, 2).

panels.rationale: The image is an MRI showing an area of upper pole irregularity and a diverticulum-like formation in the context of a case report diagnosed with Giant ectopic ureter. The image supports the diagnosis via radiological findings linked to the target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Simsir et al. Giant ectopic ureter mimicking pelvic organ prolapse: a case report.. Case reports in urology 2011. doi:10.1155/2011/304917. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: Magnetic Resonance (MR) urography showed irregularity of the upper pole of the right kidney and a diverticulum-like formation with a 12 mm stone inside (Figure 1).
